> "The Complaint of Peace" is a work written by Desiderius Erasmus in 1517. In it, Erasmus argues that the way to achieve true peace is through the teachings of Christ. He criticizes those who use violence and war to spread their ideas, saying that this is contrary to the message of Christ. Erasmus writes, "I see you, while the standard of salvation is in one hand, rushing on with a sword in the other, to the murder of your brother; and, under the banner of the cross, destroying the life of one who to the cross owes his salvation." The final paragraph of the work contains the command "resipiscite," which means a voluntary return from madness and unconsciousness.

The passage emphasizes the importance of non-violence and following the teachings of Christ in order to achieve true peace.
